A.question: Does actual POSIX flock protect JSONL record integrity across multiple independently spawned Python processes, rather than only threads, for a shared private root?
A.unit: unique synthetic capture rows across 8 processes ×40, with partial writes forced in code-adjacent offline harness

hypotheses: thread tests pass but multiprocess race corrupts lines
file system or process startup disallows shared root, invalid experiment

C.design: Use subprocess native process workers import exact SHA-verified secure_store.py, each writes deterministic 40 synthetic records and same SHA object; verify 320 unique parsed records, zero exceptions, object bytes/SHA, private mode and no .tmp leftover. Repeat >=2 independent rounds if time permits.

D.falsifier: Duplicate/missing IDs, any malformed JSON, orphan temp file, SHA mismatch, process exit nonzero; full source must match GitHub.
D.limits: Cooperating processes only, no power loss, no external hostile writer.
